observations: Single photo shows a red/orange gas cylinder with a valve, sitting in a car trunk.
No manufacturer name, capacity stamp, or serial number is legible on the cylinder body or collar.
Surface shows rust spots and chipped paint, consistent with heavy prior use.
No regulator is attached or visible in the photo.
Background clutter (car boot, boxes, duster) gives no scale reference to judge cylinder size.

claims.evidence: No weight/capacity stamp visible on the collar or body in photo 0; shape alone does not confirm 20kg versus 12.5kg or other sizes.
No import marking, foreign brand stamp, or paperwork shown in photo 0.

risks.risk: Actual capacity may be smaller than claimed (e.g. 12.5kg instead of 20kg), which changes the price bracket significantly.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the stamped capacity/manufacture date on the cylinder collar.
risks.if_unproven: priced as the smaller common size (12.5kg) rather than the claimed 20kg

risks.risk: Valve or threading may be damaged or leaking, unsafe for use.
risks.proof: Video of the valve being opened/closed and a soap-bubble leak test.

risks.risk: Corrosion/rust may have weakened the cylinder wall, a safety hazard.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the rusted areas and any pitting.
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetically and structurally worn

risks.risk: No regulator included, which buyers often expect bundled.
risks.proof: Photo showing a regulator included in the sale.
risks.if_unproven: priced as cylinder only, no regulator

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the capacity/weight stamp on the cylinder collar or body.
Photo or video showing any import/foreign brand marking to support 'tokunbo' claim.
Video of the valve opening and a leak check.
Photo confirming whether a regulator is included.
response.reason: The capacity claim (20kg) that determines which price bracket applies cannot be read from the single photo, and no stamp or scale reference is visible to confirm it.
